name: Arjun Das
title: Aspirational First-Gen Graduate
description: First in his family to complete a degree. Navigates a city that wasn't built for someone like him.
backstory: Grew up in a cramped two-room flat in Jadavpur. His father drives an auto-rickshaw; his mother stitches blouses at home. Arjun spent five years at Presidency University studying economics, sleeping through lectures he couldn't afford to fail. Now he's circling Kolkata with a fresh degree and a burning need to prove the sacrifices meant something — but the corporate world keeps asking for connections he doesn't have.
traitInteractions: High work orientation means Arjun pushes through fatigue others would yield to
Status anxiety spikes in elite spaces — Dalhousie Square offices, Flurys cafe — where he reads every glance as judgement
Frugality is not a choice; it is a survival strategy internalised as virtue
vulnerabilities: Reluctant to ask for help — fears confirming weakness

politicalPressures: Reservation debates make him simultaneously beneficiary and target of resentment
Pressure to represent 'the community' in any room he enters
Fellow graduates from affluent families dismiss his degree as quota-assisted
hiddenObligations: Promised cousin Niloy a job referral once he 'makes it'
Carries debt from coaching centre fees his parents borrowed for
insightLines: Arjun's caution isn't cowardice — every mistake costs more for someone without a safety net.
When he chose status over solidarity, he was performing a script the city taught him: respectability is survival.
His loyalty to family overrides abstract principles because family is the only institution that has never failed him.
socialContext.dilemmaProfile: Calculates risk obsessively; defers solidarity when survival is threatened
